fieldNotes.siteResolution: Given approximate coords (44.0558,-70.3475) landed in forest/golf-course terrain ~2.8km NNE of the plant; the spreadsheet address '375 Paramount Dr Raynham MA' is the Primo Brands HQ and is wrong. Web research (Wikipedia, Poland town office, CLUI land-use database, news) plus satellite resolved the active Poland Spring / Primo Brands (formerly BlueTriton / Nestle Poland Spring) bottling plant: a large single industrial building running NW-SE, accessed via a long private drive off Maine Street (ME Route 26 / 'Spring Water Road') in South Poland, ME, just east of the Poland Spring Resort golf course. Corporate address on record: 1231 Maine Street, Poland ME 04274. Locked center 44.03205,-70.35350. This is the Poland/Poland Spring plant, distinct from the separate Hollis ME plant.
fieldNotes.truckGate: TRUE, high confidence. At the south junction (~44.0277,-70.3530) where the private drive meets the yard, z20-z21 satellite shows a teardrop-shaped median island with a small structure and barrier/gate-arm markings extending laterally across both lanes; truck lanes split around the island. Classic controlled truck checkpoint (p10-pinch-z20.png, p10-booth-z21.png).
fieldNotes.guardShack: TRUE, high confidence. The median island at the gate contains a small booth-sized structure (~1-vehicle footprint, roof shadow, set between the in and out lanes) consistent with a staffed guard shack rather than the main building (p10-booth-z21.png).
fieldNotes.remoteGs: FALSE - a guard shack is present, so this is a manned booth, not a kiosk/call-box remote check-in.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Continuous loading-dock bank runs nearly the full length of the SW/south face of the ~500m-long building, with trailers backed in along its entire length (p10-dock2-z19.png, p10-dockmid-z18.png, p10-plant-z17.png). Honest estimate well into the 50+ band; ~55 used as the point figure. Banded 50+. Flagged uncertain because exact bay rhythm is hard to count over the building's full length across imagery tiles.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Two large dedicated trailer-storage yards full of parked trailers without tractors: (1) NW corner with ~3-4 diagonal rows (p10-farnw-z18.png), (2) south end with multiple long diagonal rows (p10-south-z18.png, p10-entrance-z18.png, p10-junction-z18.png). Combined well over 50 trailer stalls. Banded 50+.
fieldNotes.dropYard: TRUE - dedicated trailer-storage lots at both the NW corner and the south end, physically separate from the active dock apron.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: FALSE / low confidence - a single very long continuous dock bank on the SW face; no clearly distinct second dock cluster on a different face was confirmed, so ship/receive split could not be established from imagery.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: TRUE - large paved aprons and yard areas inside the gate and along the dock face provide interior queue/staging room before the dock doors.
fieldNotes.preGateStaging: FALSE - no dedicated paved truck-stall waiting area outside/before the gate; the long private approach drive absorbs arrivals instead.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: TRUE - long (~0.5km+) private approach drive winds through forest from the public road to the gate, plus a deep internal yard; easily holds 3+ trucks queued.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: FALSE - the gate sits deep on the private property far from any public road, with ample stacking room; a queue would not spill onto a public road.
fieldNotes.entryExitTogether: TRUE - inbound and outbound truck lanes split around the single central guard island at one entrance point (one gate complex). entryLanes/exitLanes = 1 each.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: FALSE - the gate is a tight booth-island pinch-point with limited paved width for an added express bypass lane.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: RURAL - forested South Poland ME setting bordered by woods, ponds, and the resort golf course; small-town industrial.
fieldNotes.connectivityIssue: TRUE, inferred / medium confidence - the plant is set deep in forested hills well away from dense development, so cellular coverage is plausibly weak in parts of the yard.
fieldNotes.scale: FALSE - no distinct truck-scale pad / weigh platform identified in the truck path.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: FALSE - one large connected industrial complex (NW process/warehouse block continuous with the long SE warehouse), counted as a single building.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: One primary connected industrial building running NW-SE (a wider process/warehouse block at the NW joined to the long warehouse with the dock bank); minor rooftop/utility structures not counted separately.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: ~30-40 backed in along the dock face + ~25-35 in the south drop yard + ~15-20 in the NW drop yard = ~80, approximate; mixed imagery vintages.
fieldNotes.trailerParkingCapacity: Two multi-row drop yards plus the long dock apron give a practical capacity on the order of ~120 trailers; estimate, flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~42 acres of cleared/paved footprint inside the treeline derived from the perimeter polygon; the surrounding spring/forest land is far larger but is woods, not yard. Estimate, flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.railServed: FALSE - no rail spur enters the property; access is the private road only.
fieldNotes.streetView: No Street View coverage on the private property; metadata at both the truck-gate centroid and the perimeter centroid returns ZERO_RESULTS. The nearest public-road panos (44.0268,-70.3529 / 44.0285,-70.3487, captured 2024-09) face only forest and the road, not the gate, so both zones are marked hasCoverage:false.
